significance: Francesco Maria Guazzo's Compendium Maleficarum (1608) was an Ambrosian monk's comprehensive illustrated manual of witchcraft, notable for its famous copper engravings depicting sabbath activities; the work synthesized contemporary demonological opinion and became widely influential across Catholic Europe as a practical and theological guide to witch prosecution.
source_method: Published primary source; modern edition Montague Summers trans. (1929); analyzed in Clark, Thinking with Demons (1997)
